metadata.footer: One canonical graph · contextual placements · evidence from scraper-system GitHub
metadata.subtitle: scraper-system · production digital twin
metadata.title: TAP System Atlas

availability.statusReason: Created by migration 016 with referential and temporal constraints.
availability.subtitle: Materialized recurring-event time windows
availability.summary: Expands recurring rules into concrete searchable windows without forcing product queries to evaluate recurrence logic at request time.
availability.title: event_availability_windows

browser_client.statusReason: Named as a future client in the current architecture overview; not represented by a built repository or runtime.
browser_client.subtitle: Future non-mobile execution boundary
browser_client.summary: The current task flow deliberately leaves room for a browser-based scraper beside mobile devices. No dedicated production browser-client repository exists in the organization today.
browser_client.title: Browser Scraper Client

clients_concept.statusReason: Status follows the majority of immediate canonical children. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
clients_concept.subtitle: Distributed acquisition executors
clients_concept.summary: The current client concept contains the primary Kotlin Android worker. Planned and retired client implementations remain under their lifecycle concepts by design.
clients_concept.title: Clients

deploy.statusReason: Active infrastructure repository for the Hetzner production environment.
deploy.subtitle: Infrastructure code, systemd and release orchestration
deploy.summary: The deploy repository owns production topology rather than application code: nginx, systemd, Postgres/PostGIS, directories, data-copy tools and operator runbooks. Application repositories deploy independently.
deploy.title: Deploy Control Plane

enrichments.statusReason: Created in migration 019; widened to a provider-scoped primary key in 021.
enrichments.subtitle: Mutable provider detail, media and freshness
enrichments.summary: Provider-specific POI detail is isolated from the base record so Foursquare, Facebook and web evidence can refresh independently without overwriting source identity.
enrichments.title: poi_enrichments

events.statusReason: Created in migration 001 and evolved through migration 026.
events.subtitle: Canonical geospatial event record
events.summary: One record per canonical event identity with provider-scoped deduplication, a WGS84 point, normalized category, availability model, host links, engagement, ticket and immutable image references.
events.title: events

evolution.statusReason: Status follows the majority of immediate children; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
structure: React Native client and server monorepo
evolution.subtitle: Explicit future and retired history
evolution.summary: Planned work is shown only where current or historical specifications establish a boundary. Retired components remain visible without implying production ownership.
evolution.title: Evolution

external_systems.statusReason: Status follows the majority of immediate canonical children. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
external_systems.subtitle: Providers, source evidence and delivery platforms
external_systems.summary: External sources and providers remain visible as one conceptual family while also appearing beneath the TAP component that uses them.
external_systems.title: External Systems

foursquare.statusReason: API routes, match state and enrichment tables are implemented; runtime availability depends on provider configuration.
foursquare.subtitle: POI matching and mutable detail enrichment
foursquare.summary: Frontend-server resolves or proxies place details while tap-pg separates provider match decisions from refreshable enrichment payloads.
foursquare.title: Foursquare

frontend_server.statusReason: Production service extracted from the legacy monorepo and independently deployed since Stage 9.
structure: map, product, hotel and stats routes
frontend_server.subtitle: Map, product, hotel and analytics APIs
frontend_server.summary: The product-serving control plane. It reads events, POIs, hosts and enrichments through the frontend-safe tap-pg boundary while owning links, pageviews, hotel accounts, billing and local product state in frontend.sqlite.
frontend_server.title: Frontend Server

frontend_sqlite.statusReason: Owned, migrated and health-checked by frontend-server.
frontend_sqlite.subtitle: Product-local links, traffic and hotel state
frontend_sqlite.summary: Frontend-server's private product database. It keeps mutable link payloads, analytics and account/billing state close to the product API without mixing them into canonical geospatial content.
frontend_sqlite.title: frontend.sqlite

hetzner.statusReason: Current deployment README defines this as the production layout.
hetzner.subtitle: Single-VPS runtime with separated service releases
hetzner.summary: TAP currently runs on a Hetzner VPS with separate release directories and environment files for scraper-server and frontend-server, shared data paths for SQLite, tasker, static web files and Postgres/PostGIS.
hetzner.title: Hetzner Production

hosts.statusReason: Created in migration 007 and evolved with city membership and scrape timestamps.
hosts.subtitle: Normalized organizer identity and city coverage
hosts.summary: Organizer identities are upserted from extracted host organizations and carry city coverage plus scraper freshness, allowing controlled backfills and coverage reporting.
hosts.title: hosts

hotel_admin.statusReason: Routes, account persistence and billing workflows are implemented in frontend-server.
hotel_admin.subtitle: Credentialed hotel map and billing workspace
hotel_admin.summary: A signed-in operating surface for one public hotel link per account. It lets hotels edit their map payload while subscription state gates edit access through Stripe.
hotel_admin.title: Hotel Admin

legacy_concept.statusReason: Both immediate children are legacy or retired. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
legacy_concept.subtitle: Retired implementations and historical ownership
legacy_concept.summary: Historical implementations retained for lineage, evidence and rollback context without implying current production ownership.
legacy_concept.title: Legacy

legacy_server.statusReason: Repository README says 'do not use'; current workspace marks workflows manual-only.
legacy_server.subtitle: Archived history and manual rollback only
legacy_server.summary: The former monorepo no longer owns production deployments. It remains available as historical source and a manual-only rollback path while scraper-server, frontend-server and tap-pg carry active ownership.
legacy_server.title: Legacy Server Monorepo

llm.statusReason: Implemented in tasker and used in the documented result pipeline.
structure: event, place, host and ticket data
llm.subtitle: Captured evidence to structured event result
llm.summary: Tasker applies the task-provided system message to captured page evidence and enforces a structured result. Extraction status is explicit so device, model and server failures remain operationally separable.
llm.title: LLM Extraction

mapbox.statusReason: Active dependency of web-app and frontend-server routing.
mapbox.subtitle: Globe rendering, directions and map interaction
mapbox.summary: Mapbox GL JS renders the public globe; a server-side proxy supplies directions. TAP's custom cluster drawing and invisible hit layers preserve a branded experience while accepting the WebGL integration constraints.
mapbox.title: Mapbox

matches.statusReason: Created in migration 020 with retry and provider indexes.
matches.subtitle: Provider identity-resolution lifecycle
matches.summary: Separates the act of matching a TAP POI to an external provider from the mutable payload eventually fetched for that match.
matches.title: poi_provider_matches

mobile_kotlin.statusReason: Primary client with active July 2026 changes and explicit replacement status over the React Native app.
structure: HTML, visible text, hero image, errors
mobile_kotlin.subtitle: Primary resilient Android scrape worker
mobile_kotlin.summary: The recommended production scraper client. A producer-consumer architecture combines Room persistence, connectivity awareness, foreground-service constraints, circuit breaking and a WebView capture engine so work survives unreliable device conditions.
mobile_kotlin.title: Kotlin Mobile Client

mobile_rn.statusReason: Explicitly documented as replaced by the native Kotlin application.
mobile_rn.subtitle: Original mobile scraper predecessor
mobile_rn.summary: The first mobile scraper implementation established batching, WebView capture, image extraction and wake hooks. It remains useful history, but the Kotlin client is the recommended production path.
mobile_rn.title: React Native Client

nginx.statusReason: Production routing is codified in deploy/nginx-scraper.conf.
nginx.subtitle: TLS termination and route ownership
nginx.summary: Nginx presents one public TAP origin while preserving the Stage 9 split. Scraper-specific paths go to port 9000, general product APIs go to 9001, tasker traffic goes to 8080, and the static web app owns the root.
nginx.title: Public Edge

operational_stores.statusReason: Status follows the majority of immediate canonical children. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
operational_stores.subtitle: Private persistence by failure domain
operational_stores.summary: The four local stores isolate acquisition, product, broker and device state from canonical product truth. Each store also appears beneath the component that owns its lifecycle.
operational_stores.title: Operational Stores

overture.statusReason: Overture-shaped columns and operator tooling are present in the current repositories.
overture.subtitle: Base POI identity and source attributes
overture.summary: The POI core schema is aligned to Overture Places and deployment tooling includes operator data-copy and POI support scripts.
overture.title: Overture Places

pipeline_modules.statusReason: Status follows the majority of immediate canonical children. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
pipeline_modules.subtitle: Task definition, capture and extraction
pipeline_modules.summary: The evidence-to-experience path combines runtime task assets, rendered WebView capture and structured LLM extraction. The former pipeline lens is preserved here inside the unified graph.
pipeline_modules.title: Pipeline Modules

planned_concept.statusReason: Both immediate children are planned and not yet built. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
planned_concept.subtitle: Defined boundaries not yet built
planned_concept.summary: Explicitly designed capabilities that are not represented by a current production implementation.
planned_concept.title: Planned

pois.statusReason: Created in migration 002 and extended with ranking and relation tags.
pois.subtitle: Base place identity and map-ranking record
pois.summary: A canonical place core aligned with Overture Places. Base provider evidence stays here while mutable enrichment payloads and match state live in separate tables.
pois.title: pois

postgres.statusReason: Production schema is applied by scraper-server from tap-pg migrations.
postgres.subtitle: Canonical Postgres + PostGIS product data
postgres.summary: The durable product truth: geospatial events, recurring availability, POIs, provider enrichments, identity matches and normalized hosts. GIST and GIN indexes support map, time, category and relation queries.
postgres.title: TAP Event Database

push_wake.statusReason: Specified historically but no current production FCM component or repository boundary is evidenced.
structure: signal idle clients when backlog exists
push_wake.subtitle: Wake-only signal for idle mobile workers
push_wake.summary: A wake signal can reduce reliance on periodic polling while keeping URLs and task payloads in the existing API. The original specification scoped this to notification delivery and client-token registration, not queue transport.
push_wake.title: Push Wake Channel

r2.statusReason: R2-backed immutable event image versioning is present in the canonical schema and API contract.
r2.subtitle: Versioned hero image delivery
r2.summary: Events can carry an immutable hero_image_version for CDN-backed media URLs while the database retains thumbnails and a legacy redirect fallback.
r2.title: Immutable Event Media

room.statusReason: Part of the primary Kotlin client architecture.
room.subtitle: On-device work durability
room.summary: Room persistence decouples task polling from WebView execution so the Kotlin client can recover across connectivity loss, process death, reboots and Android foreground-service limits.
room.title: Mobile Room Store

scraper_dashboard.statusReason: Embedded dashboard and supporting routes are active behind the scraper-server boundary.
structure: event and pipeline counts over time
scraper_dashboard.subtitle: Pipeline, host and ingestion control room
scraper_dashboard.summary: The scraper-server dashboard exposes operational task state, taskers, clients, cities, task types, hosts, logs and ingestion statistics. It is the operator view into the acquisition half of TAP.
scraper_dashboard.title: Scraper Operations

scraper_server.statusReason: Production service extracted from the legacy monorepo and independently deployed since Stage 9.
scraper_server.subtitle: Task creation, pipeline control and canonical ingestion
scraper_server.summary: The acquisition control plane. It creates tasks from APIs, host discovery, city backfills and Viator runners; owns operational SQLite; receives extracted results; and writes canonical events and hosts through tap-pg.
scraper_server.title: Scraper Server

scraper_sqlite.statusReason: Owned, migrated and health-checked by scraper-server.
scraper_sqlite.subtitle: Operational task and acquisition state
scraper_sqlite.summary: Scraper-server's private operational database. It intentionally holds volatile pipeline and coverage state that does not belong in the public product database.
scraper_sqlite.title: scraper.sqlite

sources.statusReason: Current primary inputs to fb_event, fb_host, fb_poi, web_poi and manual flows.
sources.subtitle: Facebook, organizer, event and place pages
sources.summary: Rendered web pages are the evidence layer for distributed scraping. Source-specific task types control URL interpretation, pre-injection and extraction behavior.
sources.title: Web Sources

stripe.statusReason: Checkout, portal, webhook and completion routes are active in frontend-server.
stripe.subtitle: Hotel subscription checkout, portal and webhooks
stripe.summary: Stripe supplies the subscription lifecycle for hotel administration. Signed webhooks are primary; a completed-checkout reconciliation path closes the gap when webhook delivery is unavailable.
stripe.title: Stripe

system_acquisition.statusReason: Represents the primary Kotlin client and current web-source capture boundary. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_acquisition.subtitle: Distributed clients and rendered source evidence
system_acquisition.summary: The acquisition spoke represents work leaving the service core for device execution and rendered web evidence. The complete task, capture, extraction and delivery pipeline now continues through its child concepts instead of a separate lens.
system_acquisition.title: Acquisition Edge

system_data.statusReason: Represents current Postgres/PostGIS and service-owned SQLite boundaries. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_data.subtitle: Canonical schema and persistence boundary
system_data.summary: The data spoke separates the shared persistence contract from service-owned operational state. The canonical chain continues farther outward through tap-pg to Postgres. Postgres is product truth; private stores remain isolated by owner and failure domain, and every real table remains directly inspectable.
system_data.title: Data Layer

system_persistence.statusReason: Conceptual grouping for the tap-pg module and canonical Postgres chain. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_persistence.subtitle: Shared database module boundary
system_persistence.summary: An intermediate data-architecture branch that keeps tap-pg farther from the TAP core than the production services while preserving its shared role across scraper and frontend.
system_persistence.title: Persistence Contract

system_products.statusReason: Represents the web app, hotel administration and operational dashboards. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_products.subtitle: Public, hotel and operator experiences
system_products.summary: The product spoke groups customer-facing and operator-facing interfaces. Product surfaces stack vertically on a shared radial anchor. The public globe, hotel workspace and two control rooms preserve the former product lens inside this unified graph.
system_products.title: Product Layer

system_runtime.statusReason: Represents the live deployment topology owned by the deploy repository. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_runtime.subtitle: Delivery infrastructure, hosting and public edge
system_runtime.summary: The runtime spoke groups deployment control, Hetzner hosting and nginx public routing independently from application ownership. Repository boundaries remain reinforced by nginx routing, separate SQLite stores, systemd and independently promoted releases.
system_runtime.title: Runtime Layer

system_services.statusReason: Represents the live scraper-server, frontend-server and tasker service layer. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
system_services.subtitle: Production control planes and task broker
system_services.summary: The service spoke groups TAP's three peer runtime services. They occupy one radial anchor and stack vertically because they are components of the same architectural kind.
system_services.title: Service Layer

tap_pg.statusReason: Standalone shared repository used by both production services.
structure: map reads, filters and admin operations
tap_pg.subtitle: Shared Postgres contract with enforced service boundaries
tap_pg.summary: The shared database module owns canonical migrations, types, query primitives and two deliberately separated public packages: scraper writes and frontend reads/admin. Its import rules prevent the Stage 9 split from drifting back into a monolith.
tap_pg.title: tap-pg

tap_root.statusReason: Conceptual root representing the live scraper-system organization and its Stage 9 production architecture. Concept status is inherited from immediate children by majority; exact ties resolve built, then planned, then legacy.
tap_root.subtitle: Event intelligence, acquisition and product delivery
tap_root.summary: The architectural root of TAP. Every lens expands outward from this point: first by responsibility, then by component hierarchy, while components of the same kind occupy a shared vertical stack.
tap_root.title: TAP System

task_assets.statusReason: Owned and deployed with scraper-server; exposed through task-type APIs.
task_assets.subtitle: Versioned scrape scripts and extraction prompts
task_assets.summary: Scraper-owned task definitions keep WebView behavior and LLM instructions out of device binaries. Pre-injection JavaScript and system prompts travel with work through tasker to the client and extraction stage.
task_assets.title: Task Type Assets

tasker.statusReason: Functional production component with SQLite persistence and a documented nine-state lifecycle.
structure: leased to and returned by device
tasker.subtitle: Mobile work broker, LLM extractor and result relay
tasker.summary: Tasker is the narrow bridge between server-created work and passive mobile scrapers. It persists a bounded queue, allocates batches, accepts captures, runs LLM extraction and forwards normalized results back to scraper-server.
tasker.title: Tasker

tasker_dashboard.statusReason: Bundled in the Go tasker and served from its root route.
tasker_dashboard.subtitle: Device queue, extraction and relay visibility
tasker_dashboard.summary: A compact monitoring surface over the mobile work queue. It shows task lifecycle states, extracted results and recent tasker logs without becoming a second system of record.
tasker_dashboard.title: Tasker Console

tasker_sqlite.statusReason: Persistent store documented and used by tasker.
structure: payload, client evidence and extracted fields
client, LLM and server relay failures
tasker_sqlite.subtitle: Bounded broker queue and extraction state
tasker_sqlite.summary: Tasker's recoverable local queue mirrors the mobile/LLM relay lifecycle. It is a transport and processing record, not the canonical event store.
tasker_sqlite.title: tasks.db

viator.statusReason: Current architecture documents Viator Phase A queueing and scraper-owned caches.
viator.subtitle: City-scoped tourism inventory sync
viator.summary: A scraper-server background runner queues synthetic city refresh work and ingests partner inventory without pretending Viator tasks are ordinary public URL submissions.
viator.title: Viator Partner API

web_app.statusReason: Built and deployed as the public static root at timeandplace.me.
web_app.subtitle: Public Mapbox event and POI experience
web_app.summary: A static, dependency-light web application that turns TAP's event, POI, route and hotel-link APIs into an explorable globe. Cluster sprites are baked in a Web Worker and the event drawer preserves selection as the user moves through clusters.
web_app.title: Events Globe

webview.statusReason: Implemented in both client generations; actively maintained in Kotlin.
webview.subtitle: DOM, visible text and hero media acquisition
webview.summary: Runs source-specific pre-injection logic, waits for page stability, captures the rendered DOM and visible evidence, extracts hero media and reports typed client failures. The source prompt and script are supplied with each task.
webview.title: WebView Capture Engine

workspace_repo.subtitle: Living architecture, skills and operator context
workspace_repo.summary: The workspace repository is the human operating layer: current architecture skills, project rules, tests, sales context and multi-repository bootstrap scripts. It is intentionally not an application monorepo.
workspace_repo.title: Workspace Knowledge
